note: Potentiators after ivacaftor (not a member): deutivacaftor approved 2024 inside vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor on HBE and FRT Ussing data, GLPG1837 and icenticaftor stopped or redirected after phase 2, navocaftor and dirocaftor without an admissible model source.
label: Cystic fibrosis (CFTR potentiators)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC); the proxy drug ivacaftor is not a tile member.
engagement.note: Ivacaftor, a non-member sibling, raised chloride secretion ~10-fold in G551D/F508del patient bronchial cells; no member-drug data yet.
engagement.short: HBE chloride rescue, sibling drug only
engagement.quote: VX-770 also increased Cl− secretion in cultured human CF bronchial epithelia (HBE) carrying the G551D gating mutation on one allele and the F508del processing mutation on the other allele by approximately 10-fold
engagement.judgement: Opening proxy: the HBE Ussing system entered the class with ivacaftor (2009), which is not a member of this tile, so product_in_model is false and the status is untested. Quote is the first 32 words of a longer abstract sentence.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (J Med Chem paywalled); whether the assay was recombinant cells or primary epithelia was not confirmed.
engagement.note: GLPG1837 opened class III mutant CFTR more than ivacaftor in Galapagos' cell assays; no patient data yet.
engagement.short: GLPG1837 beat ivacaftor in cell assay
engagement.quote: Here we describe the discovery of a novel potentiator GLPG1837, which shows enhanced efficacy on CFTR mutants harboring class III mutations compared to Ivacaftor, the first marketed potentiator.
engagement.judgement: Galapagos' own assay, scored on its own track because the system was not confirmed to be HBE. The abstract claims superiority over ivacaftor, which is the prediction the 2019 trial tests.

engagement.magnitude_basis: sweat chloride change, GLPG1837 vs ivacaftor in the same patients
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Registry NCT02707562 (first posted 2016-03-14) has no results posted; SAPHIRA2 (NCT02690519, S1251N) likewise.
engagement.note: SAPHIRA1: sweat chloride fell dose-dependently on GLPG1837 (97.7 to 68.7 mmol/L) in G551D patients, but not below their prior ivacaftor level.
engagement.short: GLPG1837 lowered sweat chloride, below ivacaftor
engagement.quote: Combined with the concentration-dependent decrease in sweat chloride concentration, results show that GLPG1837 increases CFTR activity in G551D-CF patients.
engagement.reason: Sweat chloride fell as cells predicted
engagement.judgement: Judgement call: the class-level prediction (potentiation lowers sweat chloride) held, so same, direction only. The assay's claim of greater efficacy than ivacaftor did not: sweat chloride on GLPG1837 (68.7 mmol/L) stayed above the pre-washout ivacaftor value (42.5 mmol/L) in the same patients, with 7-day dose periods a confound. Paired by me (the trial paper reports no in-vitro data); model side Van der Plas 2018.

engagement.magnitude_basis: sweat chloride change vs ELX/TEZ/IVA (−8.4 and −2.8 mmol/L) against HBE chloride-transport ordering
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level for the paper; the model side is read from FDA review NDA 218730 section 14.1.2 (HBE: D-IVA and IVA 'similar potencies'; VNZ/TEZ/D-IVA above TEZ/IVA).
engagement.note: HBE cells showed deutivacaftor equal to ivacaftor and the triple above ELX/TEZ/IVA; SKYLINE sweat chloride fell a further 8.4 and 2.8 mmol/L versus ELX/TEZ/IVA.
engagement.short: Sweat chloride fell further, as HBE predicted
engagement.quote: Vanzacaftor-tezacaftor-deutivacaftor restored CFTR function in vitro and in phase 2 trials in participants aged 18 years and older resulting in improvements in CFTR function, as measured by sweat chloride concentrations and lung function as measured by spirometry.
engagement.judgement: Dated 2025, the first public document stating both sides (the paper's background sentence; the FDA review, posted 2025, says the same). Patient data were public earlier: D-IVA monotherapy phase 2 results posted 2022-01-25 (NCT03911713: sweat chloride −6.5 mmol/L on 250 mg QD vs +0.9 on ivacaftor, ppFEV1 2.7 vs −0.8) and SKYLINE results posted 2024-06-10. Sweat chloride is read as the channel's own product (proximal). The HBE system is shared with the correctors in the triple; the potentiator's share is the D-IVA = IVA equivalence.

engagement.magnitude_basis: VTD vs ETI CFTR function: organoid swelling against sweat chloride
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Retrodiction: run after the 2024 phase 3 result was known; patient side is Keating 2025. The organoid track has no verified opening entry (its first class use, rectal organoids with ivacaftor, Dekkers 2016, was not verified within budget).
engagement.note: After SKYLINE, 62 organoid lines reproduced the clinic: the deutivacaftor triple largely comparable to ELX/TEZ/IVA with modest advantages in some genotypes.
engagement.quote: VTD provides modest genotype-specific functional advantages and enhanced CFTR maturation but is largely comparable to ETI across rare variants.
engagement.judgement: Scored retro, not same (decision 10): the organoids were run in 2025–26 against a result known since 2024, and reproduced it (modest sweat-chloride advantage, non-inferior lung function). Rodriguez Mier 2025 (doi:10.1016/j.jcf.2025.12.018) makes the same comparison explicitly for two patients (G458V, G85R) responsive to VTD but not ETI, without patient-level outcomes. Neither is a prospective prediction for a member drug.

engagement.model: Patient-derived primary nasal epithelial cells (HNE, Ussing chamber theratyping)
engagement.note: HNE cultures opened for the class with ivacaftor, lumacaftor and tezacaftor (non-members): CFTR correction correlated with FEV1 change in 8 patients.
engagement.quote: We provide the first evidence that correction of CFTR function in HNE cell cultures can predict respiratory improvement by CFTR modulators.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed 28785019, open access, epub 2017-08-07); the drugs were ivacaftor, lumacaftor and tezacaftor, none a tile member.
engagement.judgement: Opening proxy: nasal brushings cultured at air-liquid interface and read in Ussing chambers are a patient-level theratyping system distinct from the explant-derived HBE track; it entered the class with non-members, so untested.

engagement.model: Patient-derived primary nasal epithelial cells (HNE, Ussing chamber theratyping)
engagement.note: After SKYLINE, F508del/F508del HNE put vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ivacaftor standing in for deutivacaftor) above ELX/TEZ/IVA (67% vs 45% of WT), as sweat chloride had.
engagement.quote: VAN/TEZ/IVA demonstrated superior CFTR functional rescue in F508del/F508del HNECs than ELX/TEZ/IVA.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Respir Med, PubMed 41765052, epub 2026-02-27). The dish received ivacaftor, not deutivacaftor; the abstract states the clinical result (similar lung function, lower sweat chloride on VTD) as background, which is the comparison. Organoids from the same 12 patients showed no difference.
engagement.judgement: Scored retro at class level (decision 10): run after the 2024 phase 3 result, with the sibling potentiator in place of the member (product_in_model false). The ordering matched sweat chloride, not FEV1, which was non-inferior; the same paper's organoid arm did not discriminate.
engagement.magnitude_basis: HNE CFTR rescue (67% vs 45% of WT, VTI vs ETI) against the SKYLINE sweat-chloride advantage of VTD over ETI

engagement.model: Patient-derived primary nasal epithelial cells (HNE, Ussing chamber theratyping)
engagement.note: HNE from six L467F-F508del patients predicted rescue by vanzacaftor/tezacaftor; one patient given VTD on compassionate use: sweat chloride 100 to 87 mmol/L, FEV1 +220 mL.
engagement.short: One VTD patient tracked HNE prediction
engagement.quote: Of note, we report a patient treated with VTD who experienced a partial improvement in pulmonary function (FEV1 +220 mL) and exercise tolerance and a decrease of sweat Chloride concentration from 100 to 87 mmol/L.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (J Cyst Fibros, PubMed 42243036, epub 2026-06-04). n=1, compassionate use, no registry record. The dish was treated with the corrector pair (vanzacaftor/tezacaftor); whether deutivacaftor or ivacaftor was the acute potentiator is not stated, so product_in_model is null. The potentiator's share of the triple's effect cannot be separated.
engagement.judgement: Judgement call: same, patient level, with source_calls_it partial ('partial improvement'). The prediction was for the corrector pair; the member (deutivacaftor) is the potentiator in the VTD the patient received, the same sharing the draft accepts on the HBE track. A second group (doi 10.1016/j.jcf.2026.09.011) reproduced VTD rescue in L467F;F508del nasal cultures from 7 people without a patient comparison. Not scored on efficacy: a single compassionate-use FEV1 is not a trial primary endpoint.
engagement.magnitude_basis: sweat chloride 100 to 87 mmol/L in one VTD-treated patient against HNE CFTR rescue

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC); the proxy drug ivacaftor is not a tile member.
dose.note: HBE assays give an in-vitro potency but no exposure target; ivacaftor (non-member) opened the system.
dose.quote: VX-770 also increased Cl− secretion in cultured human CF bronchial epithelia (HBE) carrying the G551D gating mutation on one allele and the F508del processing mutation on the other allele by approximately 10-fold
dose.judgement: Opening proxy with a non-member drug; the HBE assay yields an EC50, not a human exposure target.

dose.confidence_note: Label section 12.1; FDA review NDA 218730 section on dose: 'In a phase 2 dose-ranging study for D-IVA (Study VX18-561-101), D-IVA 250 mg and D-IVA 150 mg QD resulted in similar absolute change from baseline in ppFEV1 compared to IVA 150 mg Q12h treatment, active control.'
dose.note: Deutivacaftor 250 mg QD was set by phase 2 dose-ranging against ivacaftor; the label says in-vitro magnitude does not track clinical magnitude.
dose.short: Dose set clinically; label disclaims in-vitro magnitude
dose.quote: For individual mutations, the magnitude of the net change over baseline in CFTR-mediated chloride transport in vitro is not correlated with the magnitude of clinical response.
dose.reason: No exposure target from the model
dose.judgement: Judgement call: kept untested. The HBE finding that D-IVA and IVA have similar potencies underpinned a once-daily regimen matched to ivacaftor exposure, and 250 mg QD then matched ivacaftor q12h in patients, so a looser reading scores same (reached, worked). Scored untested because the model stated no exposure or occupancy target, the dose came from clinical dose-ranging, and the label itself disclaims in-vitro magnitude. The review's exposure-on-curve check (phase 2 plasma concentration drawn on the HBE concentration-response) was for vanzacaftor, a corrector outside this class.

dose.model: PBPK model of deutivacaftor (CYP3A drug-interaction simulation)
dose.note: Label dose adjustments for moderate CYP3A inhibitors and inducers rest on PBPK simulation; no observed-versus-predicted check was public with the label.
dose.quote: Predicted by physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling and simulations. Data presented as geometric mean ratio and 5th to 95th percentiles of individuals in the simulated population [see Drug Interactions (7.1)].
dose.confidence_note: Label 2024-12-20, section 12.3 table footnote, verbatim in the bundle. The model's build date is not public (NDA reports T183/T322/T333; information requests answered 2024-08-23 and 2024-09-06), so first use is dated to the NDA.
dose.judgement: Opening entry: the regulator accepted PBPK-simulated exposure ratios in lieu of DDI trials for moderate CYP3A inhibitors and inducers and for children 6-11 on itraconazole (regulatory reliance on an in-silico model). Untested at the label because no predicted-versus-observed comparison was public until the review.

dose.model: PBPK model of deutivacaftor (CYP3A drug-interaction simulation)
dose.note: D-IVA PBPK model reproduced the itraconazole DDI in healthy adults (AUC ratio 12.4 predicted vs 11.1 observed); label dose adjustments remain unchecked.
dose.quote: Further, the model adequately predicted the AUCinf and Cmax ratios for the DDI with itraconazole (Study VX18-445-006) (Table 171).
dose.confidence_note: Integrated review section 14.5.2 (posted 2025), Tables 170-171 verbatim in the bundle: predicted/observed 0.93 and 1.00 (D-IVA alone), 1.31 and 1.01 (with itraconazole), DDI AUCinf ratio 12.4 vs 11.1. Study 445-006 was a phase 1 healthy-adult study (May-July 2018) with no registry record found, so registry_date is null.
dose.judgement: Scored retro, not same (decision 10): Table 170 is titled 'Used in Model Development and Validation', so Study 445-006 both informed and checked the model, and the match reproduces a known human result. The prospective predictions that set the label (fluconazole, erythromycin, verapamil, rifampin, efavirenz, children 6-11 with itraconazole) have no observed human comparison, so the track cannot score same. Dated 2025, when the review made the comparison public; the 2024 label carries only the predictions.
dose.magnitude_basis: predicted/observed D-IVA AUCinf and Cmax with and without itraconazole (0.93-1.31) and the DDI AUCinf ratio (12.4 vs 11.1)

dose.model: In-vitro human hepatic metabolism (microsomes, hepatocytes, recombinant enzymes) scaled to human PK
dose.note: Deuterated ivacaftor (CTP-656, later deutivacaftor) showed markedly enhanced in-vitro metabolic stability, the basis for a once-daily regimen; no human data at this step.
dose.quote: However, CTP-656 exhibited markedly enhanced stability when tested in vitro.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed 28611092, epub 2017-06-13). The in-vitro system (CYP-mediated oxidation; deuterium isotope effects DV 3.8, DV/K 2.2) is read from the abstract. FDA review NDA 218730 lists D-IVA metabolism studies in human liver microsomes and hepatocytes, so the system was filed.
dose.judgement: Opening entry for the one member whose pharmacokinetic design rests on an in-vitro metabolism model; the stability prediction is the model's regimen target (once daily), not an exposure number.

dose.model: In-vitro human hepatic metabolism (microsomes, hepatocytes, recombinant enzymes) scaled to human PK
dose.note: Six healthy volunteers: CTP-656 half-life 15.9 h, read by the authors as supporting once-daily dosing; whether the regimen is enough was untested.
dose.quote: The overall PK profile, including the 15.9-hour half-life for CTP-656, suggests that CTP-656 may be dosed once daily, thereby enhancing patient adherence.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the single-dose crossover in six healthy volunteers has no registry record found, so registry_date is null.
dose.judgement: Judgement call: same on healthy-volunteer PK (the brief counts it), direction only, because the abstract states no predicted half-life. Whether the once-daily exposure was enough was not known at this date; the 2024 entry carries that.
dose.magnitude_basis: in-vitro metabolic stability (no numeric half-life predicted) against the 15.9-h human half-life

dose.model: In-vitro human hepatic metabolism (microsomes, hepatocytes, recombinant enzymes) scaled to human PK
dose.note: Deutivacaftor 250 mg once daily reached and worked: phase 2 matched ivacaftor q12h on ppFEV1 and the once-daily triple was non-inferior to ELX/TEZ/IVA.
dose.quote: In a phase 2 dose-ranging study for D-IVA (Study VX18-561-101), D-IVA 250 mg and D-IVA 150 mg QD resulted in similar absolute change from baseline in ppFEV1 compared to IVA 150 mg Q12h treatment, active control.
dose.confidence_note: Review section 2 verbatim in the bundle; patient side NCT03911713 (results posted 2022-01-25) and SKYLINE (2024-06-10). Dated 2024 by the label (2024-12-20), which carries the once-daily regimen; the review was posted 2025. Paired by me: the review bridges D-IVA to IVA without citing the in-vitro stability prediction.
dose.judgement: Strengthens the 2017 same (dose rule: reached, drug worked). The model's target was a regimen (once daily), not an exposure number, so magnitude stays direction only. The review's own statement that 'A D-IVA dose regimen of 150 mg QD was predicted to provide exposure similar to IVA 150 mg q12h' came from clinical PK, not this model.
dose.magnitude_basis: once-daily regimen target against the approved 250 mg QD regimen and its phase 2 ppFEV1 match to ivacaftor q12h

dose.model: In-vitro human hepatic metabolism (microsomes, hepatocytes, recombinant enzymes) scaled to human PK
dose.note: Recombinant-UGT clearance of icenticaftor scaled by relative activity factors matched the human estimate; published after the healthy-volunteer ADME study, so a retrodiction.
dose.quote: Moreover, the predicted UGT-mediated clearance of icenticaftor, upon scaling the intrinsic clearance (CLint) with RAF, correlates well with that estimated in humans.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Pharm Res, PubMed 42343021, epub 2026-06-24). The human clearance comes from the steady-state ADME study in healthy men (doi 10.1124/dmd.124.001751, 2024); the abstract does not say whether the scaling preceded it, so retrodiction is assumed. No CF-patient PK.
dose.judgement: Scored retro (decision 10): the in-vitro scaling was published two years after the human clearance it is compared with and is framed as validating the scalars. Same system as the deuteration entries (human hepatic in-vitro metabolism scaled to human PK), a different enzyme family (UGT, not CYP).
dose.magnitude_basis: predicted versus human-estimated hepatic UGT clearance of icenticaftor; no numbers in the abstract

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC); the proxy drug ivacaftor is not a tile member.
efficacy.note: Chloride rescue in patient HBE cells taken as the proxy for benefit; opened with ivacaftor, a non-member.
efficacy.short: HBE rescue as benefit proxy, sibling drug
efficacy.quote: These results support the hypothesis that pharmacological agents that restore or increase CFTR function can rescue epithelial cell function in human CF airway.
efficacy.judgement: Opening proxy with a non-member drug (ivacaftor); untested until a member drug reached patients.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (J Med Chem paywalled); whether the assay was recombinant cells or primary epithelia was not confirmed.
efficacy.note: GLPG1837's cell-assay superiority over ivacaftor was the efficacy claim; SAPHIRA1's primary endpoint was safety, so it does not score here.
efficacy.quote: Here we describe the discovery of a novel potentiator GLPG1837, which shows enhanced efficacy on CFTR mutants harboring class III mutations compared to Ivacaftor, the first marketed potentiator.
efficacy.judgement: SAPHIRA1 (Davies 2019) had safety as its primary endpoint and lung function only returned to the pre-washout ivacaftor level, so no efficacy status from GLPG1837; icenticaftor scores the track in 2021.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: LCI2.5 and ppFEV1 vs placebo, class III/IV arm
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for both papers; the discovery paper is the sponsor's and calls its own trial a proof of concept. Patient side Kazani 2021 (doi:10.1016/j.jcf.2020.11.002, epub 2020-12-06); registry NCT02190604 results posted 2017-07-19.
efficacy.note: Icenticaftor met its LCI primary endpoint in class III/IV patients (FEV1 +6.46 points, sweat chloride −8.36 mmol/L); no effect in F508del homozygotes.
efficacy.short: Icenticaftor met LCI endpoint in class III/IV
efficacy.quote: leading to the identification of clinical development compound icenticaftor (QBW251) 33, which has subsequently progressed to deliver two positive clinical proofs of concept in patients with CF and COPD
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: dated 2021, when the model side (Grand 2021) first put the in-vitro potentiation and the trial side by side; the registry results (2017) and trial paper (2020) preceded the model paper. Scored same on the pre-specified primary (LCI2.5) in the class III/IV arm. The F508del-homozygous arm showed no efficacy although the assay potentiated F508del CFTR; no model number is public so this is not scored neg. Navocaftor (ABBV-3067) is not scored: its registry record (NCT03969888, results posted 2023-06-28) shows no ppFEV1 effect as monotherapy in F508del homozygotes (−2.2 vs −2.2 placebo; sweat chloride −8.9 vs −2.1 mmol/L) and no admissible model source was found. Dirocaftor (PTI-808) has no admissible source: CHOICES (NCT03500263) posted no results.

patient_trials.quote: Icenticaftor 450 mg bid for 14 days showed significant improvements in all endpoints versus placebo in patients with Class III and IV mutations; mean %predicted FEV1 increased by 6.46%, LCI2.5 decreased by 1.13 points

efficacy.magnitude_basis: ppFEV1 non-inferiority vs ELX/TEZ/IVA against HBE chloride-transport ordering
efficacy.confidence_note: Integrated review NDA 218730 (approval 2024-12-20, posted 2025): model side in sections 2 and 14.1.2 ('in vitro data from Ussing chamber electrophysiology experiments demonstrated greater activity for the triple drug combination'); trial side section 8.
efficacy.note: HBE put the deutivacaftor triple above ELX/TEZ/IVA and D-IVA equal to IVA; SKYLINE met ppFEV1 non-inferiority (difference 0.2 points, 95% CI −0.7 to 1.1).
efficacy.short: ppFEV1 non-inferior, as HBE ordering predicted
efficacy.quote: Both Trials 102 and 103 demonstrated the noninferiority of VNZ/TEZ/D-IVA to ELX/TEZ/IVA with respect to the ppFEV1 through 24 weeks.
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: same, direction only. The HBE ordering (VNZ/TEZ/D-IVA > TEZ/IVA; D-IVA = IVA) predicted at least ELX/TEZ/IVA-level efficacy and the primary endpoint delivered non-inferiority, with superiority only on sweat chloride (−8.4 and −2.8 mmol/L). A stricter reading calls the 'greater activity' claim over-predicted on FEV1, where the comparator is near-ceiling. Year 2024: registry results posted 2024-06-10 and the label/approval of 2024-12-20 carry both sides; the review itself was posted in 2025.

patient_trials.quote: Vanzacaftor-tezacaftor-deutivacaftor is non-inferior to elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor in terms of FEV1 % predicted, and is safe and well tolerated.
Vanzacaftor-tezacaftor-deutivacaftor is non-inferior to elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor in terms of FEV1 % predicted, and is safe and well tolerated.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: responder status by genotype (FRT ≥10% of normal) vs ppFEV1 subgroup
efficacy.confidence_note: Integrated review NDA 218730 section 2 and Table 2; the label (section 12.1) sets the FRT threshold at ≥10% of normal and says in-vitro magnitude does not correlate with clinical magnitude, so the model predicts who responds, not how much.
efficacy.model: FRT cells carrying each CFTR variant (Ussing chamber)
efficacy.note: FDA took FRT responsiveness for 259 variants with no trial; the 42 trial subjects with 23 in-vitro-responsive non-F508del variants responded like the rest.
efficacy.short: FRT-picked genotypes responded; 259 added on cells
efficacy.quote: The subgroup analysis of these subjects was limited by sample size but was consistent with the overall population and supportive of the noninferiority of VNZ/TEZ/D-IVA to ELX/TEZ/IVA in this population.
efficacy.reason: FDA relied on FRT; subgroup consistent
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level track: FRT cells predict genotype responsiveness and the regulator accepted them in lieu of trials (regulatory_reliance true; 31 variants not responsive to ELX/TEZ/IVA in FRT were excluded). The only patient check is the 42-subject subgroup, 'limited by sample size'. The track opens with the ivacaftor precedent (2012–2017 label expansions, non-member), so model_first_use_year is 2012 with no separate opening entry.

efficacy.model: Patient-derived primary nasal epithelial cells (HNE, Ussing chamber theratyping)
efficacy.note: FEV1 correlation shown with non-member modulators only; no member-drug trial has an HNE-predicted primary endpoint.
efficacy.quote: The level of CFTR correction in HNE cultures significantly correlated with the FEV1 change at 6 months in 8 patients treated with CFTR modulators.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed 28785019, open access); the 8 patients received ivacaftor, lumacaftor or tezacaftor, none a tile member.
efficacy.reason: No member-drug trial endpoint vs HNE
efficacy.judgement: Stays untested through 2026: the only member-drug patient datum on this track is one compassionate-use FEV1 (+220 mL, Capurro 2026), not a trial primary endpoint; the HIT-CF/CHOICES selection used organoids, not HNE.

safety.magnitude_basis: cataract adverse events on the deutivacaftor arm against juvenile-rat cataracts
safety.confidence_note: The member's own juvenile toxicology was not run: 'Juvenile animal toxicology studies for IVA and TEZ were previously reviewed under NDA 203188 and NDA 212273'; deutivacaftor is bridged to ivacaftor. Causality of the patient cataracts is not established.
safety.model: Rat toxicology (juvenile and adult, ivacaftor program)
safety.note: Juvenile-rat cataracts from the ivacaftor program carried onto the deutivacaftor label; cataract adverse events occurred on the deutivacaftor arm at rates similar to ELX/TEZ/IVA.
safety.short: Rat cataracts; cataract AEs on D-IVA arm
safety.quote: Cataracts have been observed in subjects, particularly pediatric subjects, treated with IVA monotherapy and in juvenile rat toxicology studies with IVA.
safety.judgement: Judgement call: same, direction only, with product_in_model false because the rats received ivacaftor, the non-member isotopologue. The review's Table 46 lists cataract (2) and cortical cataract (3) on the VNZ/TEZ/D-IVA arm and finds rates 'similar between treatment arms', and keeps the warning. Liver: rat liver findings in the ivacaftor and vanzacaftor programs preceded the transaminase and DILI boxed warning, consistent rather than a miss; no source frames a harm the animals should have shown and missed, so no contra.
